key_idea: Lower-bound the distance and testability through a locally minimal distance: a cycle that is not locally minimal can be shortened by one local move, so every lightweight syndrome can be peeled off greedily. This is then combined with small-set edge expansion of lifted Ramanujan graphs and their squares, applied to a lifted product of Tanner codes.
reason: The local-minimality lemma is short and transparent. A single argument gives both the quantum distance and local testability, which makes the reduction elegant. Much of the rest relies on expansion bookkeeping, such as the harmonic-sum estimate for Γ², and on parameter tuning for the rate and testability constants, so routine estimates carry a large share of the work.
recognized: Panteleev–Kalachev, 'Asymptotically Good Quantum and Locally Testable Classical LDPC Codes' (lifted product of Tanner codes)
